title.value: Safeguard is a Double-edged Sword: Denial-of-service Attack on Large Language Models

abstract.value: Safety is a paramount concern of large language models (LLMs) in their open deployment. To this end, safeguard methods aim to enforce the ethical and responsible use of LLMs through safety alignment or guardrail mechanisms. However, we found that the malicious attackers could exploit false positives of safeguards, i.e., fooling the safeguard model to block safe content mistakenly, leading to a new denial-of-service (DoS) attack affecting LLM users. Specifically, through software or phishing attacks on user client software, attackers insert a short, seemingly innocuous adversarial prompt into user prompt templates in configuration files. This prompt triggers safeguard rejections of nearly all user requests from the client while remaining hidden in the user interface and non-trivial to detect. By designing an optimization process that utilizes gradient and attention information, our attack can automatically generate seemingly safe adversarial prompts, approximately only 30 characters long, that universally block over 97% of user requests on Llama Guard 3. The attack presents a new dimension of evaluating LLM safeguards focusing on false positives, different from the classic jailbreak.

primary_area.value: foundation or frontier models, including LLMs
